name: Arlington Memorial Bridge
note: Roadway is bike-legal end to end and one authority throughout; the midpoint heuristic must not split it.

name: Key Bridge
note: The roadway is a legal, ordinary climb, not barred - riders use it every day. sidepath_only marks it anyway: it is a narrow bridge with no shoulder and no way off mid-span, so a mass ride still has to be kept to the sidewalk provision rather than the traffic lane. Do not read sidepath_only as a legality claim; roadway_bicycle_legal is the legality claim.

name: Chain Bridge
note: A standard, bike-legal climb out of Georgetown - not barred. Five-foot sidewalk with no way off mid-span is why sidepath_only is still set: a mass ride cannot use the roadway safely even though an individual rider legally can.

name: George Mason Memorial Bridge
note: One of three parallel structures once lumped together as "14th Street Bridge"; not one bridge and not one answer, which is why this is now three rows. This one carries I-395's southbound freeway lanes: OSM carries bicycle=no on the roadway and there is no sidepath on this particular structure, so this is a bar-outright case, not a sidepath-only one. Community working knowledge, unverified against a real extract.

name: Rochambeau Bridge
note: The second of the three former "14th Street Bridge" spans, carrying I-395's northbound freeway lanes. Same shape as George Mason Memorial Bridge: bicycle=no on the roadway, no sidepath on this structure, barred outright. Community working knowledge, unverified against a real extract.

name: Arland D. Williams Jr. Memorial Bridge
osm_names: Arland D. Williams Jr. Memorial Bridge
note: The third of the three former "14th Street Bridge" spans - the Metrorail bridge, which is also where the Mount Vernon Trail connection actually is. No roadway lane a bicycle could use, so roadway_bicycle_legal is false; the shared-use path is the only and the intended crossing, so sidepath_only is true. Community working knowledge, unverified against a real extract.

name: Woodrow Wilson Bridge path
note: The roadway carries I-95/I-495 and bicycle=no in OSM; the shared-use path is a separate structure and the only crossing. row_owner is best-known community knowledge, not confirmed against a current authority list - MDTA operates the bridge itself, but ownership of the connecting right-of-way on the Virginia side (the Jones Point sliver, the short-crossing case) may sit with VDOT instead.

name: Sousa Bridge (Pennsylvania Avenue SE)
note: Anacostia crossing usable by a mass ride.

name: 11th Street Bridge
note: Local span carries bikes; the freeway spans do not.

name: Frederick Douglass Memorial Bridge
note: South Capitol Street's Anacostia crossing; a bike-legal roadway with its own protected provision, not a sidepath-only case. Community working knowledge, unverified against a real extract.

name: Whitney Young Memorial Bridge
osm_names: Whitney M. Young Jr. Memorial Bridge
note: A bike-legal roadway. Community working knowledge, unverified against a real extract - included on the reviewer's word that it belongs in this set, without an independently confirmed location or spelling.

name: Benning Road Bridge
note: Benning Road's Anacostia crossing; a bike-legal roadway. Community working knowledge, unverified against a real extract.

name: Theodore Roosevelt Bridge
note: Carries I-66 across the Potomac; bicycle=no in OSM and no sidepath on the structure, so this is barred outright rather than sidepath-only. Tagged highway=trunk, which MOTOR_ONLY does not catch, so the no-trail variant depends entirely on the rm:bridge_bicycle mechanism (resolve_bridge_bicycle_legality) to keep a mass ride off it - there is no highway-class fallback here. Community working knowledge, unverified against a real extract.

name: American Legion Bridge
police: Montgomery County Police / Fairfax County Police
note: Carries the Capital Beltway (I-495) across the Potomac near Cabin John. No bicycle or pedestrian provision of any kind - not sidepath-only, no access. Community working knowledge, unverified against a real extract.
